sources: United Nations: list of Member States (193) and of non-member observer States (Holy See, State of Palestine), as published by the UN.

UN Statistics Division: Standard country or area codes for statistical use (M49) for 3-digit codes, regions, sub-regions and intermediate regions. The 'subregion' field uses the intermediate region where M49 defines one (e.g. Eastern Africa, Caribbean, South America), otherwise the sub-region.
ISO 3166-1 (alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric codes) for country identifiers; numeric codes coincide with M49 codes. Taiwan is not listed separately in M49, so its ISO 3166-1 numeric code is used.

National constitutions and official-language legislation, as summarised in each entry's notes, for de jure official languages. Where the provision has not been checked, the entry says so and needsReview is true.
BCP 47 language tags as used by Unicode CLDR, matching content/registry/languages.json.

countries.name: Algeria
countries.notes: Constitution: Arabic is the national and official language; Tamazight became a national and official language in the 2016 revision. 'ber' stands in for Tamazight (several varieties, e.g. Kabyle). French is widely used, including in higher education, but has no official status. Everyday spoken Arabic is Algerian Arabic (arq).

countries.name: Egypt
countries.notes: Everyday spoken Arabic is Egyptian Arabic (arz); schooling uses Modern Standard Arabic.

countries.name: Libya
countries.notes: The 2011 Constitutional Declaration names Arabic as official and guarantees the linguistic rights of Amazigh, Tebu and Tuareg communities. Everyday spoken Arabic is Libyan Arabic (ayl).

countries.name: Morocco
countries.notes: 2011 Constitution: Arabic and Amazigh (Tamazight) are official. French is widely used in education and business without official status. Everyday spoken Arabic is Moroccan Arabic (ary).

countries.name: Sudan
countries.notes: The 2005 Interim National Constitution made Arabic and English official working languages. Sudan has since had transitional constitutional arrangements (2019 Constitutional Document and later amendments) whose language provisions have not been checked. Everyday spoken Arabic is Sudanese Arabic (apd).

countries.name: Tunisia
countries.notes: Arabic is the constitutional language of the state. French is widely used in education (notably secondary and higher mathematics) without official status. Everyday spoken Arabic is Tunisian Arabic (aeb).

countries.name: Burundi
countries.notes: Kirundi is the national language; Kirundi and French are official, and a 2014 language law added English. Swahili is also widely used.

countries.name: Comoros
countries.notes: Constitution: official languages are Shikomori (Comorian, the national language), French and Arabic. 'zdj' (Shingazidja) is used as a stand-in code for Shikomori, which has several island varieties. Primary Lumenary language set to French because it is the main written language of schooling; to be reviewed.

countries.name: Djibouti
countries.notes: Constitution: French and Arabic are official. Somali and Afar are widely spoken.

countries.name: Eritrea
countries.notes: No de jure official language. The 1997 constitution (never implemented) affirms the equality of Eritrean languages. Tigrinya, Arabic and English function as working languages; English is the main medium of secondary and higher education, while mother-tongue instruction is used in early primary school.

countries.name: Ethiopia
countries.notes: The 1995 Constitution gives all Ethiopian languages equal state recognition and makes Amharic the working language of the Federal Government; regional states choose their own working languages (e.g. Afaan Oromo in Oromia). In 2020 the government announced additional federal working languages (reported as Afaan Oromo, Tigrinya, Somali and Afar); implementation status not verified. Secondary mathematics is generally taught in English.

countries.name: Kenya
countries.notes: 2010 Constitution, Art. 7: Kiswahili is the national language; Kiswahili and English are the official languages. English is the main medium of instruction for mathematics beyond the early primary years, so an English pathway is equally important.

countries.name: Madagascar
countries.notes: Malagasy is the national language; Malagasy and French are official. French is widely used in secondary mathematics.

countries.name: Malawi
countries.notes: No official language is designated in the constitution as far as has been checked. English is used in government and as the medium of instruction after the early primary years; Chichewa is the national language and the most widely spoken.

countries.name: Mauritius
countries.notes: The constitution does not designate an official language; it makes English the language of the National Assembly (French may also be used there). English is the main medium of school examinations; French dominates the media; Mauritian Creole (mfe) is the most widely spoken home language.

countries.name: Mozambique
countries.notes: Constitution: Portuguese is official. Many Bantu languages are widely spoken; bilingual primary schooling exists in some areas.

countries.name: Rwanda
countries.notes: Kinyarwanda is the national language; official languages are Kinyarwanda, English, French and (since 2017) Swahili. English is the main medium of instruction after the early primary years.

countries.name: Seychelles
countries.notes: The constitution designates Creole, English and French as the national languages; they are treated here as official. English is the main language of schooling.

countries.name: Somalia
countries.notes: The 2012 Provisional Constitution makes Somali (Maay and Maxaa-tiri) the official language and describes Arabic as the second language; whether Arabic should be recorded as official needs checking.

countries.name: South Sudan
countries.notes: The 2011 Transitional Constitution makes English the official working language and declares all indigenous languages national languages. Juba Arabic is a widely used lingua franca.

countries.name: Uganda
countries.notes: Constitution (as amended in 2005): English is the official language and Swahili the second official language. Luganda is the most widely spoken language. English is the main medium of instruction.

countries.name: United Republic of Tanzania
countries.notes: The constitution does not designate an official language as far as has been checked. Kiswahili is the national language and the main language of government and of public primary schooling; English is the main medium of secondary and higher education. A 2021 amendment to the Interpretation of Laws Act made Kiswahili the language of the courts.

countries.name: Zambia
countries.notes: Constitution: English is the official language. Seven regional languages (Bemba, Nyanja, Tonga, Lozi, Lunda, Kaonde, Luvale) are used in early schooling.

countries.name: Zimbabwe
countries.notes: Partial list. Section 6 of the 2013 Constitution recognises 16 official languages: Chewa, Chibarwe, English, Kalanga, Koisan, Nambya, Ndau, Ndebele, Shangani, Shona, sign language, Sotho, Tonga, Tswana, Venda and Xhosa. Only those present in the language registry are listed (Chewa=ny, Shangani=ts, Ndebele=nd). Shona is the most widely spoken; English is the main medium of instruction.

countries.name: Angola
countries.notes: Constitution: Portuguese is official. Umbundu, Kimbundu, Kikongo and other languages are widely spoken.

countries.name: Cameroon
countries.notes: Constitution: English and French are official languages of equal value. Most of the population lives in francophone regions.

countries.name: Central African Republic
countries.notes: Sango and French have been the official languages; Sango is spoken by nearly the whole population, while French dominates written education. A new constitution was adopted recently; its language provisions have not been re-checked for this registry. (2023 constitution)

countries.name: Chad
countries.notes: French and Arabic are official. Chadian Arabic is a widespread lingua franca. A new constitution was adopted recently; its language provisions have not been re-checked for this registry. (2023 constitution)

countries.name: Congo
countries.notes: French is official; Lingala and Kituba (Munukutuba) are national languages.

countries.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
countries.notes: 2006 Constitution: French is official; Kikongo (Kituba), Lingala, Swahili and Tshiluba are national languages.

countries.name: Equatorial Guinea
countries.notes: Spanish, French and (since 2010-2011) Portuguese are official. Spanish is the main language of schooling.

countries.name: Gabon
countries.notes: French is official. A new constitution was adopted recently; its language provisions have not been re-checked for this registry. (2024 constitution)

countries.name: Sao Tome and Principe
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: Portuguese is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Botswana
countries.notes: No official language is designated in the constitution as far as has been checked. English is the language of government and the main medium of instruction beyond the first years of primary school; Setswana is the national language and is spoken by most of the population.

countries.name: Eswatini
countries.notes: 2005 Constitution: siSwati and English are official.

countries.name: Lesotho
countries.notes: Constitution: Sesotho and English are official.

countries.name: Namibia
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 3: English is the official language; other languages (e.g. Oshiwambo, Afrikaans, Otjiherero, German) may be used in schools and regionally.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.notes: Twelve official languages: the eleven listed in Section 6 of the 1996 Constitution plus South African Sign Language (added in 2023). isiZulu is the most common home language; English is the most widely shared language across the country and the main medium of instruction from the later primary years, hence the primary choice. isiZulu, isiXhosa and Afrikaans pathways are high priorities.

countries.name: Benin
countries.notes: Constitution: French is official. Fon, Yoruba and many other national languages are spoken.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
countries.notes: Partial list. A constitutional revision begun in December 2023 (Art. 35) makes the national languages recognised by law the official languages and makes French and English working languages. The registry lists the three most widely spoken national languages (Mooré, Dioula, Fulfulde); the full legal list has not been checked. French remains the main medium of schooling.

countries.name: Cabo Verde
countries.notes: Constitution: Portuguese is official; the state is to promote conditions for officialising Cape Verdean Creole (kea), the everyday language.

countries.name: Côte d'Ivoire
countries.notes: Constitution: French is official. Dioula is a major lingua franca.

countries.name: Gambia
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. Mandinka, Wolof and Fula are widely spoken.

countries.name: Ghana
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. Akan (Twi/Fante), Ewe, Ga and Dagbani are among the widely spoken languages.

countries.name: Guinea
countries.notes: Partial list. The constitution approved by referendum in September 2025 is reported to make eight national languages official alongside French (reported to include Pular/Fula, Maninka, Susu and Kissi). The full list and article text have not been checked. French is the main language of schooling and the only one shared nationally, hence the primary choice.

countries.name: Guinea-Bissau
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: Portuguese is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. Guinea-Bissau Creole (Kriol) is the main lingua franca.

countries.name: Liberia
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Mali
countries.notes: Partial list. 2023 Constitution, Art. 31: the national languages are the official languages, and French is the working language. The 13 national languages are Bamanankan, Bomu, Bozo, Dogon, Fulfulde, Hassaniya, Mamara, Maninkakan, Soninke, Songhoy, Syenara, Tamasheq and Khassonké; only those in the language registry are listed. Bambara is the most widely spoken; French remains the main medium of secondary and higher education.

countries.name: Mauritania
countries.notes: Constitution: Arabic is official; Arabic, Pulaar, Soninke and Wolof are national languages. Everyday Arabic is Hassaniya (mey). French is widely used in education.

countries.name: Niger
countries.notes: The Refoundation Charter published on 31 March 2025 makes Hausa the national language and English and French the working languages, and lists further 'spoken languages of Niger' (e.g. Zarma-Songhai, Fula, Kanuri, Arabic). It uses the terms 'national' and 'working' rather than 'official', so officialLanguages is left empty. Hausa is the most widely spoken language; French remains the main medium of schooling.

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.notes: The 1999 Constitution has no general official-language clause; Section 55 provides for National Assembly business in English (and in Hausa, Igbo and Yoruba when arrangements are made). English is universally treated as official and is the medium of instruction beyond the early primary years. Whether this counts as de jure needs review. Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo and Nigerian Pidgin are major languages.

countries.name: Senegal
countries.notes: Constitution: French is official; Wolof, Pulaar, Serer, Diola, Mandinka, Soninke and other codified languages are national languages. Wolof is the most widely spoken.

countries.name: Sierra Leone
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. Krio is the main lingua franca.

countries.name: Togo
countries.notes: French is official; Ewe and Kabiye are national languages. A new constitution was adopted recently; its language provisions have not been re-checked for this registry. (2024 constitution)

countries.name: Antigua and Barbuda
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Bahamas
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Barbados
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Cuba
countries.notes: 2019 Constitution: Spanish is the official language.

countries.name: Dominica
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. Dominican Kwéyòl (French-based creole) is widely spoken.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
countries.notes: Constitution: Spanish is the official language.

countries.name: Grenada
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Haiti
countries.notes: 1987 Constitution: Haitian Creole and French are official. Creole is spoken by virtually the whole population; French has historically dominated written schooling.

countries.name: Jamaica
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. Jamaican Creole (Patwa) is the everyday language of most people.

countries.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Saint Lucia
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. Saint Lucian Kwéyòl (French-based creole) is widely spoken.

countries.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Trinidad and Tobago
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Belize
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. Spanish and Belizean Kriol are widely spoken.

countries.name: Costa Rica
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 76: Spanish is the official language.

countries.name: El Salvador
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 62: Spanish is the official language.

countries.name: Guatemala
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 143: Spanish is official. The National Languages Law (2003) recognises Mayan, Garifuna and Xinka languages; Kʼicheʼ (quc) is the most widely spoken Mayan language.

countries.name: Honduras
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 6: Spanish is the official language.

countries.name: Mexico
countries.notes: No de jure official language at federal level. The General Law of Linguistic Rights of Indigenous Peoples (2003) recognises Spanish and the Indigenous languages as national languages with equal validity. Spanish is the de facto language of government and most schooling. Nahuatl (nah) and Yucatec Maya (yua) are in the registry.

countries.name: Nicaragua
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 11: Spanish is official; the languages of the Caribbean Coast communities (e.g. Miskito) are also official in the autonomous regions.

countries.name: Panama
countries.notes: Constitution: Spanish is the official language.

countries.name: Argentina
countries.notes: No official language is designated at national level in the constitution; Spanish is used de facto. Guaraní is co-official in Corrientes province. Absence of a statutory designation should be confirmed.

countries.name: Bolivia (Plurinational State of)
countries.notes: Partial list. 2009 Constitution, Art. 5: Spanish and 36 Indigenous languages are official; only Spanish, Quechua, Aymara and Guaraní are listed here because the others are not yet in the language registry.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 13: Portuguese is the official language. Brazilian Sign Language (Libras) is legally recognised; some municipalities have co-officialised Indigenous or immigrant languages.

countries.name: Chile
countries.notes: The constitution does not designate an official language; Spanish is used de facto. Mapudungun (arn) and other Indigenous languages are spoken. Absence of a statutory designation should be confirmed.

countries.name: Colombia
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 10: Spanish is official; the languages of ethnic groups are also official in their territories.

countries.name: Ecuador
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 2: Spanish is the official language; Spanish, Kichwa and Shuar are official languages of intercultural relations; other ancestral languages are official in their areas. Kichwa is a Quechuan language and is recorded as qu; Shuar is not yet in the language registry.

countries.name: Guyana
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. Guyanese Creole is widely spoken.

countries.name: Paraguay
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 140: Spanish and Guaraní are official. Guaraní is spoken by most of the population; Spanish dominates written schooling.

countries.name: Peru
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 48: Spanish is official, and in areas where they predominate so are Quechua, Aymara and the other Indigenous languages, as provided by law.

countries.name: Suriname
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: Dutch is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. Sranan Tongo (srn) is the main lingua franca.

countries.name: Uruguay
countries.notes: No official language is designated in the constitution as far as has been checked; Spanish is used de facto. Uruguayan Sign Language is legally recognised. Should be confirmed.

countries.name: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of)
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 9: Spanish is official; Indigenous languages are official for Indigenous peoples.

countries.name: Canada
countries.notes: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms (s. 16) and the Official Languages Act: English and French. Inuktitut and other Indigenous languages are official in some territories (e.g. Nunavut).

countries.name: United States of America
countries.notes: English was designated the official language by Executive Order 14224 (signed 1 March 2025). This is an executive order, not a statute: Congress has not enacted an official-language law, and the order states that it creates no enforceable rights. Many states have their own official-language laws (Hawaii recognises Hawaiian). Spanish is widely spoken.

countries.name: Kazakhstan
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 7: Kazakh is the state language; Russian is officially used on an equal basis in state organisations and local self-government.

countries.name: Kyrgyzstan
countries.notes: Constitution: Kyrgyz is the state language; Russian is an official language.

countries.name: Tajikistan
countries.notes: Constitution: Tajik is the state language; Russian is the language of interethnic communication.

countries.name: Turkmenistan
countries.notes: Constitution: Turkmen is the state language.

countries.name: Uzbekistan
countries.notes: Constitution: Uzbek is the state language. Russian is widely used; Karakalpak is official in Karakalpakstan.

countries.name: China
countries.notes: The Law on the Standard Spoken and Written Chinese Language (2000) designates Putonghua and standardised (Simplified) characters as the national common language and script. Minority languages (e.g. Uyghur, Tibetan, Mongolian, Zhuang, Korean) are used in autonomous areas.

countries.name: Democratic People's Republic of Korea
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: Korean (Chosŏnmal) is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Japan
countries.notes: No law designates an official language; Japanese is the de facto national language. The Ainu Promotion Act (2019) recognises the Ainu as an Indigenous people; Ainu (ain) is in the registry.

countries.name: Mongolia
countries.notes: Constitution: Mongolian is the official language. Cyrillic is the everyday script; a 2015 law provides for reintroducing the traditional Mongolian script in official use.

countries.name: Republic of Korea
countries.notes: The Framework Act on the National Language makes Korean the national language.

countries.name: Brunei Darussalam
countries.notes: Constitution: Malay is the official language. English is widely used in education.

countries.name: Cambodia
countries.notes: Constitution: Khmer is the official language.

countries.name: Indonesia
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 36: Indonesian is the state language. Javanese and Sundanese are among hundreds of regional languages.

countries.name: Lao People's Democratic Republic
countries.notes: Constitution: Lao is the official language and script.

countries.name: Malaysia
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 152 and the National Language Act: Malay is the national and official language. English is widely used; Chinese- and Tamil-medium primary schools exist.

countries.name: Myanmar
countries.notes: 2008 Constitution, Art. 450: Myanmar (Burmese) is the official language.

countries.name: Philippines
countries.notes: 1987 Constitution, Art. XIV: Filipino is the national language; Filipino and English are official. Mathematics is commonly taught in English.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 153A: Malay, Mandarin Chinese, Tamil and English are official; Malay is the national language. English is the medium of instruction for mathematics.

countries.name: Thailand
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: Thai is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Timor-Leste
countries.notes: Constitution, Section 13: Tetum and Portuguese are official; Indonesian and English are working languages. Portuguese is widely used in written schooling; the primary choice of Tetum (the most widely spoken) should be reviewed with educators.

countries.name: Viet Nam
countries.notes: 2013 Constitution, Art. 5: Vietnamese is the national language (recorded here as official).

countries.name: Afghanistan
countries.notes: The 2004 Constitution made Pashto and Dari official. Since August 2021 the de facto authorities have not applied that constitution; current legal status is unclear, though both languages remain in use. Dari is the most widely used lingua franca.

countries.name: Bangladesh
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 3: Bangla is the state language.

countries.name: Bhutan
countries.notes: Constitution: Dzongkha is the national language (recorded as official). English is the main medium of instruction, including for mathematics; an English pathway is equally important.

countries.name: India
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 343 and the Official Languages Act 1963: Hindi (in Devanagari) is the official language of the Union, and English continues to be used for official purposes. The 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule (all in the registry) are 'scheduled', not Union official; states have their own official languages. Mathematics is taught in many languages, with English very common in secondary and higher education.

countries.name: Iran (Islamic Republic of)
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 15: Persian is the official language. Azerbaijani, Kurdish, Arabic, Balochi and other languages are widely spoken.

countries.name: Maldives
countries.notes: Constitution: Dhivehi is the national language (recorded as official). English is the main medium of instruction in schools.

countries.name: Nepal
countries.notes: 2015 Constitution, Art. 7: Nepali in Devanagari is the official language of the nation; provinces may adopt additional official languages. Maithili and Bhojpuri are widely spoken.

countries.name: Pakistan
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 251: Urdu is the national language and is to be used for official purposes; English may be used officially until replaced. Punjabi (pa-Arab), Pashto, Sindhi, Saraiki and Balochi are widely spoken.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
countries.notes: Constitution: Sinhala and Tamil are official and national languages; English is the link language.

countries.name: Armenia
countries.notes: Constitution: Armenian is the state language.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
countries.notes: Constitution: Azerbaijani is the state language.

countries.name: Bahrain
countries.notes: Constitution: Arabic is the official language. Everyday spoken Arabic includes Gulf (afb) and Bahraini varieties.

countries.name: Cyprus
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 3: Greek and Turkish are official.

countries.name: Georgia
countries.notes: Constitution: Georgian is official (and Abkhaz in Abkhazia).

countries.name: Iraq
countries.notes: 2005 Constitution, Art. 4: Arabic and Kurdish are official; Turkmen and Syriac are official in areas where their speakers are concentrated. Kurdish is recorded as ckb (Sorani); Kurmanji/Badini (ku) is also used. Everyday Arabic is Mesopotamian Arabic (acm).

countries.name: Israel
countries.notes: Basic Law: Israel as the Nation-State of the Jewish People (2018): Hebrew is the state language; Arabic has a 'special status', and the law states that it does not harm the status Arabic had before the law.

countries.name: Jordan
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 2: Arabic is the official language. Everyday spoken Arabic is Levantine (apc).

countries.name: Kuwait
countries.notes: Constitution: Arabic is the official language.

countries.name: Lebanon
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 11: Arabic is the official national language; a law determines when French may be used. Mathematics is widely taught in French or English.

countries.name: Oman
countries.notes: Basic Statute: Arabic is the official language.

countries.name: Qatar
countries.notes: Constitution: Arabic is the official language.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.notes: Basic Law of Governance, Art. 1: Arabic is the language of the state.

countries.name: Syrian Arab Republic
countries.notes: Arabic has been the official language under successive constitutions. Following the change of government in December 2024 a constitutional declaration was issued in 2025; its language provision has not been checked.

countries.name: Türkiye
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 3: Turkish is the language of the state.

countries.name: United Arab Emirates
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 7: Arabic is the official language. English is very widely used, including in education.

countries.name: Yemen
countries.notes: Constitution: Arabic is the official language.

countries.name: Belarus
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 17: Belarusian and Russian are state languages. Russian is the more widely used in daily life and schooling.

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 3: Bulgarian is the official language.

countries.name: Czechia
countries.notes: No constitutional clause; Czech is the official language by statute (e.g. the Administrative Procedure Code).

countries.name: Hungary
countries.notes: Fundamental Law, Art. H: Hungarian is the official language.

countries.name: Poland
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 27: Polish is the official language. Kashubian is a recognised regional language.

countries.name: Republic of Moldova
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 13: the state language was named 'Moldovan' until a 2023 law replaced it with 'Romanian' throughout the legislation. Gagauz and Russian are widely used.

countries.name: Romania
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 13: Romanian is the official language. Hungarian is widely used in some regions.

countries.name: Russian Federation
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 68: Russian is the state language; republics may establish their own state languages (e.g. Tatar, Bashkir, Chechen, Sakha).

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 6 and the State Language Act: Slovak is the state language. Hungarian is a significant minority language.

countries.name: Ukraine
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 10: Ukrainian is the state language.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.notes: No general law designating an official language has been identified; Danish is the de facto official language. German is a recognised minority language in South Jutland; Faroese and Greenlandic are official in the Faroe Islands and Greenland.

countries.name: Estonia
countries.notes: Constitution, § 6: Estonian is the official language.

countries.name: Finland
countries.notes: Constitution, § 17: Finnish and Swedish are the national languages. Sami languages are official in the Sami homeland.

countries.name: Iceland
countries.notes: Act No. 61/2011: Icelandic is the national and official language; Icelandic Sign Language is recognised.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 8: Irish is the national and first official language; English is recognised as a second official language. English is the more widely spoken; Irish-medium schools (Gaelscoileanna) teach mathematics in Irish.

countries.name: Latvia
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 4: Latvian is the official language. Latgalian is protected as a historical variety; Livonian as an Indigenous language.

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 14: Lithuanian is the state language.

countries.name: Norway
countries.notes: Language Act (2021): Norwegian is the main national language, with two equal written standards (Bokmål and Nynorsk); Sami is an Indigenous language of equal value; Kven, Romani, Romanes and Norwegian Sign Language are protected. Sami is official in Sami administrative areas.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.notes: Language Act (2009): Swedish is the principal language. Finnish, Meänkieli, Sami, Romani Chib and Yiddish are official national minority languages; Swedish Sign Language has a protected status.

countries.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
countries.notes: No de jure official language at UK level; English is the de facto language. Welsh is official in Wales (Welsh Language (Wales) Measure 2011); Scottish Gaelic is an official language of Scotland (Gaelic Language (Scotland) Act 2005); Irish and Ulster Scots have recognised status in Northern Ireland (Identity and Language (Northern Ireland) Act 2022).

countries.name: Albania
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 14: Albanian is the official language.

countries.name: Andorra
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 2: Catalan is the official language. Spanish and French are widely used; French- and Spanish-system schools operate alongside Andorran schools.

countries.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
countries.notes: The state-level constitution (Dayton Agreement, Annex 4) does not designate an official language; Bosnian, Croatian and Serbian are official in the entities and used at state level. They are mutually intelligible standard varieties; Latin and Cyrillic scripts are both official. The primary choice of Bosnian is provisional; a learner should be offered all three.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 13: Croatian in Latin script is the official language; minority languages may be official locally.

countries.name: Greece
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: Greek is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Holy See
countries.notes: UN non-member observer State. Latin is the official language of the Holy See; Vatican City State legislation and administration use Italian. The legal basis and exact status of each have not been verified.

countries.name: Italy
countries.notes: Law 482/1999: Italian is the official language; it also protects historical minority languages (e.g. German in South Tyrol, French in Aosta Valley, Slovene, Ladin, Sardinian, Friulian).

countries.name: Malta
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 5: Maltese is the national language; Maltese and English are official. Mathematics is commonly taught using English.

countries.name: Montenegro
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 13: Montenegrin is the official language; Serbian, Bosnian, Albanian and Croatian are also in official use; Cyrillic and Latin are equal. The primary choice is provisional; Montenegrin and Serbian are mutually intelligible and a learner should be offered both.

countries.name: North Macedonia
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 7: Macedonian in Cyrillic is official; the 2019 Law on the Use of Languages extends official use of Albanian at national level.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 11: Portuguese is the official language. Mirandese has official recognition (1999 law).

countries.name: San Marino
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: Italian is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Serbia
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 10: Serbian and the Cyrillic script are in official use; Latin script is also very widely used (sr-Latn). Minority languages are official in some municipalities (e.g. Hungarian in Vojvodina).

countries.name: Slovenia
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 11: Slovenian is official; Italian and Hungarian are also official in the municipalities where those communities live.

countries.name: Spain
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 3: Castilian (Spanish) is the official language of the state; other languages are co-official in their autonomous communities (Catalan/Valencian, Basque, Galician, and Aranese Occitan in Catalonia). Much schooling in those communities is in the co-official language.

countries.name: Austria
countries.notes: Federal Constitutional Law, Art. 8: German is the official language; Croatian, Slovene and Hungarian are official regionally.

countries.name: Belgium
countries.notes: Constitution and language laws: Dutch, French and German are official, each in its own language area (Brussels is bilingual Dutch/French). Dutch has the most speakers.

countries.name: France
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 2: French is the language of the Republic; Art. 75-1 recognises regional languages as part of France's heritage.

countries.name: Germany
countries.notes: No constitutional clause; German is the official language by statute (e.g. Administrative Procedure Act § 23, Courts Constitution Act § 184). Danish, Frisian, Sorbian, Romani and Low German are protected minority/regional languages.

countries.name: Liechtenstein
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 6: German is the national and official language.

countries.name: Luxembourg
countries.notes: Law of 24 February 1984: Luxembourgish is the national language; French is the language of legislation; French, German and Luxembourgish are administrative languages. French was chosen as primary because it is the most widely known language among residents; German is used for early literacy. This choice is provisional.

countries.name: Monaco
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 8: French is the official language.

countries.name: Netherlands (Kingdom of the)
countries.notes: General Administrative Law Act: Dutch is the official language; Frisian is also official in the province of Fryslân. Papiamentu and English are official in the Caribbean Netherlands.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.notes: Federal Constitution, Art. 4: German, French, Italian and Romansh are national languages; Art. 70: German, French and Italian are official languages of the Confederation, and Romansh is official for communication with Romansh speakers. Cantons set their own official languages. Schooling is in Standard German in German-speaking cantons, though Swiss German dialects are spoken.

countries.name: Australia
countries.notes: No de jure official language; English is the de facto national language. Many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages are spoken (examples in the registry: Warlpiri, Pitjantjatjara, Kriol).

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.notes: Māori (Māori Language Act 1987; Te Ture mō Te Reo Māori 2016) and New Zealand Sign Language (NZSL Act 2006) are official by statute. English has no statutory official status but is the de facto main language, hence deFactoLanguages and the primary choice. Māori-medium schooling (kura kaupapa Māori) teaches mathematics in Māori.

countries.name: Fiji
countries.notes: The 2013 Constitution recognises English, iTaukei (Fijian) and Fiji Hindi; whether all three are formally 'official' should be checked. English is the main medium of instruction.

countries.name: Papua New Guinea
countries.notes: The constitution does not designate official languages as far as has been checked, though English, Tok Pisin and Hiri Motu are commonly described as official (and PNG Sign Language was reportedly added in 2015). English is the main medium of instruction; Tok Pisin is the most widely used lingua franca. Primary choice should be reviewed with educators.

countries.name: Solomon Islands
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. Pijin (pis) is the main lingua franca.

countries.name: Vanuatu
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. 3: Bislama is the national language; the official languages are Bislama, English and French; the principal languages of education are English and French.

countries.name: Kiribati
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English and Gilbertese is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Marshall Islands
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: Marshallese and English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Micronesia (Federated States of)
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. Each state has its own main languages (e.g. Chuukese, Pohnpeian, Kosraean, Yapese).

countries.name: Nauru
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: Nauruan and English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. English is the main written language of schooling.

countries.name: Palau
countries.notes: Constitution, Art. XIII: Palauan and English are the official languages.

countries.name: Samoa
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: Samoan and English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Tonga
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: Tongan and English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Tuvalu
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: Tuvaluan and English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: State of Palestine
countries.notes: UN non-member observer State. Amended Basic Law, Art. 4: Arabic is the official language. Everyday spoken Arabic is Levantine (apc).

countries.name: China, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
countries.notes: Special Administrative Region of China. Basic Law, Art. 9 and the Official Languages Ordinance: Chinese and English are official. Written Chinese uses Traditional characters; Cantonese (yue) is the main spoken language and the usual oral medium of Chinese-medium schools.

countries.name: China, Macao Special Administrative Region
countries.notes: Special Administrative Region of China. Basic Law, Art. 9: Chinese and Portuguese are official. Cantonese is the main spoken language.

countries.name: Taiwan
countries.notes: Listed as 'other' because it is neither a UN member nor a UN observer. ISO 3166-1 lists it as TW/TWN/158 with the English short name 'Taiwan, Province of China'; UN M49 does not list it separately, so the numeric code is the ISO 3166-1 code and the region is assigned geographically. No single official language is designated; the National Languages Development Act (2019) treats the natural languages of Taiwan's peoples (including Mandarin, Taiwanese Hokkien, Hakka, Indigenous Formosan languages, Matsu Eastern Min and Taiwan Sign Language) as national languages. Mandarin in Traditional characters is the main language of government and schooling.

countries.name: Puerto Rico
countries.notes: Territory of the United States. Spanish and English are official (Law 1 of 1993). Spanish is the main language of public schooling.

countries.name: Greenland
countries.notes: Self-governing part of the Kingdom of Denmark. Greenland Self-Government Act (2009): Greenlandic is the official language. Danish is widely used, including in secondary education.

countries.name: Faroe Islands
countries.notes: Self-governing part of the Kingdom of Denmark. Home Rule Act (1948): Faroese is the principal language; Danish must be taught well and may be used in public affairs.

countries.name: Åland Islands
countries.notes: Autonomous region of Finland. The Act on the Autonomy of Åland makes Swedish the sole official language.

countries.name: Isle of Man
countries.notes: British Crown Dependency. English is the de facto language; Manx Gaelic is used ceremonially and in a Manx-medium primary school. No legal designation has been checked.

countries.name: New Caledonia
countries.notes: French overseas collectivity with special status. French is official; the Nouméa Accord recognises the Kanak languages (about 28) as languages of education and culture.

countries.name: French Polynesia
countries.notes: French overseas collectivity. French is official; Tahitian and other Polynesian languages may be used under the 2004 organic law.

countries.name: Guam
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English and Chamorro is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: American Samoa
countries.notes: Legal basis not verified: English and Samoan is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry. Territory of the United States.

countries.name: Cook Islands
countries.notes: Self-governing state in free association with New Zealand; not a UN member. Te Reo Maori Act 2003: Cook Islands Māori and English are official.

countries.name: Niue
countries.notes: Self-governing state in free association with New Zealand; not a UN member. Legal basis not verified: Niuean and English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.

countries.name: Réunion
countries.notes: Overseas department and region of France. French is official; Réunion Creole is the everyday language of most residents.

countries.name: Mayotte
countries.notes: Overseas department of France. French is official; Shimaore (a Comorian variety) and Kibushi (a Malagasy variety) are widely spoken.

countries.name: French Guiana
countries.notes: Overseas department and region of France. French is official; French Guianese Creole, Maroon creoles and Indigenous languages are widely spoken.

countries.name: Martinique
countries.notes: Overseas department of France. French is official; Martinican (Antillean) Creole is widely spoken.

countries.name: Aruba
countries.notes: Constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Papiamento and Dutch are official (2003 ordinance). Dutch has been the main language of secondary schooling; the primary choice should be reviewed with educators.

countries.name: Curaçao
countries.notes: Constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Papiamentu, Dutch and English are official (2007). The primary choice should be reviewed with educators.

countries.name: Bermuda
countries.notes: British Overseas Territory. Legal basis not verified: English is the language of government and schooling and is commonly listed as official, but the constitutional or statutory provision has not been checked for this registry.
